summary.short: NYC rules for employers and employment agencies using automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) in hiring or promotion. An AEDT may not be used if its bias audit is over one year old. Employers must publish audit results and distribution dates, and give advance notice to candidates and employees.
summary.long: The rule adds Subchapter T to Chapter 5 of Title 6 of the Rules of the City of New York, governing automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) used by employers and employment agencies to screen candidates for employment or employees for promotion. An employer or employment agency may not use or continue to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since its most recent bias audit (§ 5-301(a)). Bias audits by an independent auditor must calculate selection or scoring rates and impact ratios by sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories, and may use historical data or, if insufficient, test data (§§ 5-301, 5-302). Before use, the employer must publish on its employment webpage the date of the latest audit, a summary of results and the AEDT distribution date (§ 5-303). For city-resident candidates and employees, notice must be given at least 10 business days before use, including instructions for requesting an alternative selection process or accommodation where available (§ 5-304). Employers must also disclose their AEDT data retention policy, the types of data collected and the data source, and answer written requests within 30 days (§ 5-304(d)). The document contains no penalty or enforcement provisions.

notes: The document is Section 1 of a rule amendment only. It contains no adoption, filing or effective date and does not name the issuing agency, although the registry metadata names the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection. The duties and definitions it relies on in Administrative Code §§ 20-870 and 20-871 are not reproduced. The rule's examples omit data ('[AEDT data and calculations from example omitted]'). The operative thresholds (one-year bias audit window, 2% exclusion in § 5-301(d), 10 business days notice in § 5-304(b)-(c), 6-month posting in § 5-303(c), 30-day response in § 5-304(d)(2)) are not coded in this pass, as only relations, entities and notes were requested.

definitions.defined_in: Administrative Code of the City of New York § 20-870 (incorporated by § 5-300 of this instrument)

evidence.quote: “Automated employment decision tool” or “AEDT” means “Automated employment decision tool” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code where the phrase “to substantially assist or replace discretionary decision making” means:

definitions.defined_in: Administrative Code of the City of New York § 20-870

evidence.quote: “Bias audit” means “Bias audit” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code.

“Candidate for employment” means a person who has applied for a specific employment position by submitting the necessary information or items in the format required by the employer or employment agency.

“Category” means any component 1 category required to be reported by employers pursuant to subsection (c) of section 2000e-8 of title 42 of the United States Code as specified in part 1602.7 of title 29 of the Code of Federal Regulations

definitions.defined_in: Administrative Code of the City of New York § 20-870

evidence.quote: “Employment decision” means “Employment decision” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code.
“Employment agency” means “Employment agency” as defined by 6 RCNY § 5-249.
“Historical data” means data collected during an employer or employment agency’s use of an AEDT to assess candidates for employment or employees for promotion.
“Independent auditor” means a person or group that is capable of exercising objective and impartial judgment on all issues within the scope of a bias audit of an AEDT.

“Impact ratio” means either (1) the selection rate for a category divided by the selection rate of the most selected category or (2) the scoring rate for a category divided by the scoring rate for the highest scoring category.

definitions.term: Machine learning, statistical modeling, data analytics, or artificial intelligence

evidence.quote: “Machine learning, statistical modeling, data analytics, or artificial intelligence” means a group of mathematical, computer-based techniques:
“Scoring Rate” means the rate at which individuals in a category receive a score above the sample’s median score, where the score has been calculated by an AEDT.
“Screen” means to make a determination about whether a candidate for employment or employee being considered for promotion should be selected or advanced in the hiring or promotion process.
“Selection rate” means the rate at which individuals in a category are either selected to move forward in the hiring process or assigned a classification by an AEDT.
“Simplified output” means a prediction or classification as specified in the definition for “machine learning, statistical modelling, data analytics, or artificial intelligence.”
“Test data” means data used to conduct a bias audit that is not historical data.
“Distribution date” means the date the employer or employment agency began using a specific AEDT.

obligations.summary: Employer or employment agency may not use or continue to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since the most recent bias audit of the AEDT.
obligations.conditional_on: More than one year since the most recent bias audit of the AEDT

evidence.quote: An employer or employment agency may not use or continue to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since the most recent bias audit of the AEDT.

obligations.summary: A bias audit must, at a minimum, calculate selection rates and impact ratios by sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories, and indicate the number of individuals in unknown categories. Under § 5-301(c), where an AEDT scores candidates, the bias audit must instead calculate the median score, scoring rates, impact ratios by the same category types, and unknown-category counts.

evidence.quote: a bias audit must, at a minimum

obligations.summary: Independent auditor may exclude from the impact ratio calculations a category representing less than 2% of the data used for the bias audit; the summary of results must then include the auditor's justification and the number of applicants and scoring or selection rate for the excluded category.
obligations.conditional_on: Category represents less than 2% of the data used for the bias audit

evidence.quote: an independent auditor may exclude a category that represents less than 2% of the data being used for the bias audit from the required calculations for impact ratio.

obligations.summary: A bias audit conducted under § 5-301 must use historical data of the AEDT, which may come from one or more employers or employment agencies. An employer may rely on a bias audit using other employers' historical data only if it provided its own historical data to the auditor or has never used the AEDT.

evidence.quote: A bias audit conducted pursuant to section 5-301 of this Chapter must use historical data of the AEDT.

obligations.summary: Employer or employment agency may rely on a bias audit that uses test data if insufficient historical data is available for a statistically significant audit; the summary of results must then explain why historical data was not used and how the test data was generated and obtained.
obligations.conditional_on: Insufficient historical data available to conduct a statistically significant bias audit

evidence.quote: an employer or employment agency may rely on a bias audit that uses test data if insufficient historical data is available to conduct a statistically significant bias audit.

obligations.summary: Before using an AEDT, employer or employment agency in the city must publicly post on the employment section of its website the date and summary of results of the most recent bias audit (including data source, unknown-category counts, applicant numbers, selection or scoring rates and impact ratios) and the AEDT distribution date; a link is permitted if clearly identified. The summary and distribution date must stay posted for at least 6 months after the latest use of the AEDT for an employment decision.
obligations.applies_from: Before the use of an AEDT
obligations.conditional_on: Employer or employment agency in the city

evidence.quote: Before the use of an AEDT, an employer or employment agency in the city must make the following publicly available on the employment section of their website in a clear and conspicuous manner

Code § 20-871(b)(1) and (2), an employer or employment agency may notify NYC candidates for employment and employees considered for promotion at least 10 business days before AEDT use, by website notice, job posting, written policy (for employees), or U.S. mail or e-mail. Methods are listed as alternatives.

enforcement.note: The document sets out bias audit, data, publication and notice requirements (§§ 5-300 to 5-304) but states no fines, penalties or other sanctions. It refers to §§ 20-870 and 20-871 of the Administrative Code, which are not reproduced in this text, so any sanction regime there is outside this document.
